messages:
matt: FYI customer seeing a spike of 504s and a retry storm. They use our Go SDK v1.3.2, per-request ctx.WithTimeout, and a shared http.Client with no Timeout. Connections pile up, CLOSE_WAIT grows. Anyone seen 504s -> retries -> more 504s?
priya: two quick suspects: response bodies not drained/closed, and transport keepalive settings. Do we have a repro or any goroutine/fd metrics?
matt: customer log snippet: "read tcp 10.0.0.5:42134->1.2.3.4:443: context deadline exceeded" plus steady rise in CLOSE_WAIT. They sit behind a proxy and use http2.
ingrid: CLOSE_WAIT rising usually means resp.Body isn't closed. With Go + http2 + ctx cancel, sockets can get stuck if body isn't read/closed. Ask them to ensure resp.Body.Close() or io.Copy(ioutil.Discard, resp.Body) on cancel.
priya: also check http.Transport. Safe defaults we recommend:
````
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns:        100,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
````
If they never drain bodies, idle pool fills and new dials block causing timeouts.
matt: they set client.Timeout=0 and rely on ctx.WithTimeout. Is that OK?
sam: it's common. client.Timeout enforces an overall deadline inside net/http; ctx.WithTimeout controls per-request lifecycle. The trouble is if ctx is canceled before reading body, connection reuse fails.
priya: nuance: canceling a ctx before reading the body doesn't implicitly drain/close it for you. For keepalive reuse you must either read to EOF or call Close() to return the connection to the pool. On cancel, underlying TCP can sit half-closed until server closes it -> fd leak.
ingrid: for heavy-retry clients safer options: 1) always drain+close response body on cancel, 2) shorten IdleConnTimeout so bad sockets are reaped faster, or 3) add per-route inflight limits to avoid retry storms.
matt: I'll try to reproduce quickly: local server delays body write, client uses shared Transport + http2, send request with ctx.WithTimeout(1s) and cancel, loop many times and watch fd count.
priya: also toggle HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2; http2 cancel semantics can behave differently with keepalives and proxies.
matt: repro plan:
- test server that delays body for 10s
- client shared transport + http2 enabled
- do req with ctx.WithTimeout(1s) and intentionally not read body to reproduce leak
Code snippet I plan to run:
````
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1*time.Second)
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", srv.URL, nil)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if resp != nil {
  // intentionally NOT reading body to reproduce leak
}
cancel()
````
ingrid: good. Then try:
````
if resp != nil {
  io.Copy(ioutil.Discard, resp.Body)
  resp.Body.Close()
}
````
and compare FD/goroutine behavior.
priya: mitigation notes: upgrade Go runtime if <1.18; older go versions had rougher http2 cancel handling. Also our Go SDK v1.3.2 had a wrapper that delayed body.Close in some error paths — we fixed that in v1.4.0 to always discard/close on cancel.
matt: I'll ask the customer to try two quick mitigations: (A) ensure code drains+closes bodies, (B) temporarily set Transport.MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2 to limit idle pool, and report goroutine/fd stats.
support-bot: Created support ticket INC-2026-421 and escalated to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
oncall: pinging eng-runtime and eng-infra for follow-up. @ingrid @priya can you take engineering follow-up?
ingrid: taking it. I'll run the repro and if confirmed we'll patch the Go SDK to close/discard on cancel and add docs about client.Transport vs client.Timeout semantics.
priya: FYI for customers behind proxies/load balancers: upstream slow responses + client cancel can create half-closed chains and cause 502/504s at the proxy. Keepalives + http2 are more brittle in that chain.
matt: customer also had no per-route inflight cap, so retries piled up. Recommend per-route semaphore or rate limiter to prevent retry storms.
sam: quick SDK POC: wrap Do() and defer a func that drains resp.Body when resp != nil so cancel paths don't leak. Also ensure retries respect context cancellation to avoid duplicate in-flight requests.
priya: please collect the repro FD/goroutine graphs and if the drain/close fix stops the leak we can push v1.4.0 patch and advise the customer. :thumbsup:
matt: will update INC-2026-421 after customer tests. closing loop soon.
